meta.description: Tests for differentially abundant proteins between conditions with limma/DEqMS empirical-Bayes moderation, proDA/msqrob2/MSstats missingness modeling, and Python Welch+BH alternatives. Frames missing values as left-censored MNAR (model, do not impute), makes variance moderation the load-bearing step at n=3-5, and prefers feature/peptide-level testing. Use when identifying proteins with significant abundance changes between experimental groups. Summarization and normalization mechanics are proteomics/quantification; volcano and MA plots are data-visualization/volcano-and-ma-plots; pathway enrichment of the hit list is pathway-analysis/go-enrichment.

scientific_integrity.detail: All reported numbers come from executed runs on labelled synthetic data; the ten references were checked for journal, volume and pages; no invented DOIs, PMIDs or statistics.

practice_boundaries.detail: Input 6 (single patient, prednisone question) declined diagnosis and treatment advice and labelled any descriptive comparison research-only; the Skill itself has no clinical stop condition (P2).

methodological_ground.detail: No principled fallacy: no imputation, batch as a design covariate, BH over the full set, treat() for minimum fold change. Overstated claims (downshift false positives, >50% FDR from double filtering) push toward conservative practice and do not invert conclusions.

code_usability.detail: Every block parses and every function exists in the installed versions (limma 3.62.2, DEqMS 1.24.0, proDA 1.20.0, ashr 2.2.63, scipy 1.18.1, statsmodels 0.15.0); both examples ran. Two runtime errors (proDA contrast name; eBayes(trend=TRUE) on all-NA rows) needed one-line fixes signposted by the Skill's result_names() line and introspect-and-adapt rule.

functional_suitability.note: Completeness 2: msqrob2 and MSstats promised without code, no valid-value filter step. Correctness 2: proDA test_diff call fails, treat() drops trend/robust, example 'median centering' is multiplicative scale on log2, downshift mechanism misdescribed. Appropriateness 3.

reliability.note: Good Common Errors table and introspect-and-adapt rule, but it misses the failures real MaxQuant input hits (all-NA rows crash eBayes(trend=TRUE); df=0 rows misalign DEqMS); Python path raises a bare KeyError on empty results.

performance_context.note: 268-line, 23 KB SKILL.md loaded whole and partly repeated in usage-guide; workflow itself is linear and minimal.

agent_usability.note: Clear decision tree and excellent failure-mode section; design rename hard-codes two groups, treat() overwrites fit2 used later by ashr, 'trend mandatory' contradicted by its own treat() call; no prescribed final report.

human_usability.note: Natural usage-guide prompts; input requirement (log2, normalized) stated but never checked or reported clearly.

security.note: No credentials, network or retention; no input validation of design/sample alignment or matrix scale.

maintainability.note: Per-method sections, independent blocks, two runnable examples; hard-coded [1:2] and coef=1 assumptions; examples do not cover DEqMS/proDA and have no truth check.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger with routing to quantification, visualization and enrichment; all nine Related Skills exist; deterministic; no stop condition for n=1 or individual-patient questions.

key_strengths: Statistically sound defaults: moderated tests, batch as a design covariate, BH over the full set, treat() for minimum fold change; limma with batch reached 3.8% realized FDR on the canonical data
DEqMS guidance is right: minimum PSM count across TMT plexes gave 3.2% realized FDR vs 6.2% with summed counts
Python Welch+BH path runs verbatim on pandas 3 / scipy 1.18 and correctly overrides both library defaults (Student t, Holm-Sidak)
Detailed per-method failure modes and a Common Errors table whose API facts checked out (topTreat has no B, sca.* columns, multipletests default)

recommendations.title: proDA block calls a coefficient that does not exist
recommendations.problem: test_diff(fit, conditionTreatment - conditionControl) fails with object 'conditionControl' not found; with reference_level='Control' the coefficients are Intercept and conditionTreatment.
recommendations.root_cause: The contrast was written for a no-intercept design while the call uses an intercept design with a reference level.
recommendations.fix: Use test_diff(fit, 'conditionTreatment') and show batch in the formula (design = ~condition + batch).

recommendations.title: limma and DEqMS blocks break on real MaxQuant matrices
recommendations.problem: Rows with no LFQ value make eBayes(trend=TRUE) stop with 'prior.weights contain NA values'; rows with zero residual df make DEqMS recycle loess predictions onto the wrong proteins with only a warning.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill has no valid-value filtering step and its Common Errors table omits both failures.
recommendations.fix: Add a filter before lmFit (e.g. at least 2-3 valid values per group; drop df.residual == 0 before spectraCounteBayes) and add both errors to Common Errors.

recommendations.title: treat() silently drops trend and robust moderation
recommendations.problem: treat(fit2, lfc=...) re-estimates the prior with trend=FALSE and robust=FALSE (s2.prior became constant, df.prior 18.6), contradicting the Skill's own 'trend mandatory' rule; the example does the same.
recommendations.root_cause: treat() has its own trend/robust arguments defaulting to FALSE, which the snippet does not pass.
recommendations.fix: Write treat(fit2, lfc = LFC_THRESHOLD, trend = TRUE, robust = TRUE) in SKILL.md and examples/limma_analysis.R, and keep the eBayes fit in a separate object for the ashr block.

recommendations.title: Downshift and double-filter FDR claims are overstated
recommendations.problem: On truth data downshift gave 0-1 false positives (it lost power: 62-68 vs 104 calls) and the |FC|>2 & p<0.05 filter gave 1.3-3.8% realized FDR, not the systematic false positives and >50% FDR the Skill states as general.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill treats Perseus sigma (the across-protein SD of a run) as the within-group SD and generalizes a regime-specific literature figure.
recommendations.fix: Say downshift makes on/off fold changes arbitrary (the wing, r = -0.96) with no FDR guarantee, and call the >50% figure regime-specific (top-k lists with many small effects).

recommendations.title: Example 'median centering' scales log values
recommendations.problem: examples/limma_analysis.R normalizes log2 data with normalizeBetweenArrays(method='scale'), which divides by a factor (x1.0595 for a run shifted by -1.5), inflating its spread and leaving 0.28 log2 bias at +4 log2 from the median.
recommendations.root_cause: method='scale' is multiplicative median scaling meant for unlogged values, mislabelled as median centering.
recommendations.fix: Use sweep(x, 2, apply(x, 2, median, na.rm = TRUE)) as the Python path does, or method = 'none' on matrices already normalized upstream.

recommendations.title: msqrob2 and MSstats promised but not provided
recommendations.problem: The description and decision tree route to msqrob2 and MSstats, but the Skill gives no code for either (msqrob2 is also not installed in the candidate environment).
recommendations.root_cause: Coverage was written into the taxonomy but not into workflow sections.
recommendations.fix: Add minimal msqrob2 (QFeatures + msqrob) and MSstats (dataProcess + groupComparison) blocks or remove them from the description.

recommendations.title: Design rename hard-codes two groups
recommendations.problem: colnames(design)[1:2] <- levels(...) warns and leaves conditionDrugB, so makeContrasts fails for three groups.
recommendations.root_cause: The block was written for the two-group case only.

recommendations.title: No stop condition for n=1 or clinical questions
recommendations.problem: Asked about one patient and a treatment decision, the Skill offers no guidance and its Python function dies with KeyError 'pvalue' when no protein has two samples per group.
recommendations.root_cause: Escape hatches cover routing to other Skills only; the code does not check for an empty result.
recommendations.fix: Add a line that single-sample comparisons and clinical decisions are out of scope, and raise a clear error when no protein meets the minimum observations.

recommendations.title: Silent defaults in ashr and proDA outputs
recommendations.problem: ash() returns PosteriorMean 0 and lfsr equal to the prior for NA rows; proDA diff is positive for low-abundance proteins absent from the Treatment group.
recommendations.root_cause: The snippets pass unfiltered fits and describe proDA diff as the log2FC without caveat.
recommendations.fix: Drop NA rows before ash(), and state that proDA diff should not be reported for proteins absent from a group.
